issues.legal_issue: A tenant who, after a genuine dispute over who is entitled to receive rent or an unjustified refusal by the landlord to accept it, deposits rent in court may be treated as having paid it and protected from eviction for rent arrears.
material_facts: After the original landlord died, several heirs succeeded to ownership, leaving the tenant uncertain who was entitled to receive rent.
The tenant attempted to tender rent to one heir, who refused it, and the tenant was permitted to deposit rent in court.
After receiving the landlords’ demand notice, the tenant offered in writing to pay the rent if the heir confirmed willingness to accept it, and said otherwise he would deposit it in court.
The landlords did not respond to that offer and instead sued for eviction; the tenant deposited the arrears in court.
The courts below ordered eviction for default, but the Supreme Court found that the tenant had been ready and willing to pay and that his court deposits were justified.
issues.conclusion: The tenant’s deposits were justified and were to be treated as payment to the landlords; he was not in arrears so as to be evicted on that ground. The appeal was allowed, the orders below were set aside, and the eviction suit was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 20(2)(a), 20(4), 30(1) and 30(6), 39 and 40 of the U.P. Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972, a tenant ordinarily must pay rent to the landlord and may face eviction for qualifying arrears after demand and failure to pay within the prescribed time. But where a bona fide dispute exists about the person entitled to receive rent, or the landlord unjustifiably refuses to accept it, the tenant may use the court-deposit procedure; a deposit within that procedure is deemed payment to the landlord. The Act’s tenant-protective scheme should be interpreted to advance its purpose rather than by a narrow or technical approach. No earlier cases are cited.

rule.if: eviction_claim_based_on_rent_arrears and tenant_ready_to_pay and (bona_fide_dispute_over_rent_recipient or landlord_refused_tender) and tenant_offered_payment_to_landlord and landlord_did_not_respond_to_offer and tenant_deposited_rent_in_court

predicates.eviction_claim_based_on_rent_arrears: The landlord brought a proceeding seeking eviction of the tenant on the basis of unpaid rent.
predicates.tenant_ready_to_pay: The tenant remained willing to pay rent to the person entitled to receive it.
predicates.bona_fide_dispute_over_rent_recipient: There was a genuine uncertainty or dispute about which claimant was entitled to receive the rent.
predicates.landlord_refused_tender: The landlord or a person claiming entitlement to receive rent refused the tenant’s tender.
predicates.tenant_offered_payment_to_landlord: The tenant told the landlord or claimant that the tenant was willing to pay the rent.
predicates.landlord_did_not_respond_to_offer: The landlord or claimant did not respond to the tenant’s offer to pay.
predicates.tenant_deposited_rent_in_court: The tenant deposited the rent in court after the tender or offer was not accepted.

issues.definition: When an eviction claim is based on rent arrears, a willing tenant who faces a genuine dispute about the recipient or a refusal of tender, offers payment, receives no response, and deposits the rent in court is not evictable for those arrears.
